Model Unit-Level Outcomes from Sequence or Network Predictors

Source: R/outcome_model.R
outcome_model.Rd

outcome_model() fits a regression of a unit-level outcome on predictor columns (pattern indicators, topological features from simplicial_features(), or any other numeric covariates) and returns a tidy effect table with confidence intervals and multiplicity-corrected p-values. A two-valued outcome gets a logistic regression and a numeric one a linear regression; a group column adds a random intercept per group, and select = "split" chooses the predictors on one half of the data and fits them on the other.

Each effect is conditional on the other terms in the model; for a two-valued outcome, the odds ratio is the factor by which the odds of the outcome value coded 1 change per unit of the predictor. The p-values are corrected across every term except the intercept, the adjust covariates included. A predictor that counts events also measures how long the unit was observed; enter that exposure through adjust.

Usage

outcome_model(
  data,
  outcome,
  predictors,
  group = NULL,
  adjust = NULL,
  family = c("auto", "binomial", "gaussian"),
  select = c("none", "split"),
  n_select = 10L,
  correction = "BH",
  ci_level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_outcome_model'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_outcome_model'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_outcome_model'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per unit of analysis. Rows with a missing value in the outcome, a predictor, an adjust covariate or the group column are left out; when none is left, an error of class nestimate_empty_model_frame is raised. A column that is not in data raises an error.

outcome

The outcome column. With family = "auto", an outcome with two distinct values is modelled with the binomial family (the second value in sort order, level order for a factor, or TRUE, coded 1) and any other with the gaussian family, which needs a numeric outcome.

predictors

The predictor columns. A predictor that is not numeric (a logical column included; convert it with as.integer()) or has no variance in the complete rows is dropped and listed in the result; when every predictor is dropped, an error of class nestimate_no_variance is raised.

group

A grouping column, such as the actor the units are nested in. When lme4 is installed, a random intercept per group is added, the right treatment for units nested in actors. lme4 is a suggested package: without it the random intercept is dropped, a warning of class nestimate_no_lme4 is raised, and a plain stats::glm() is fitted. Default NULL.

adjust

Covariates entered before the predictors. Use it for exposure: a unit observed longer contains more of every pattern, so an unadjusted effect can be volume in disguise. Default NULL.

family

The model family: "auto" (default) reads it from the outcome, "binomial" and "gaussian" force one. "binomial" codes the second-smallest outcome value (or TRUE) as 1 and every other value as 0, so give it a two-valued outcome.

select

How the predictors are chosen: "none" (default) fits all of them; "split" ranks them on a random half of the rows by the absolute z or t statistic of a one-predictor glm() (without adjust or group), keeps the best n_select, and fits the reported model on the other half.

n_select

The number of predictors kept when select = "split". Default 10. Ignored otherwise.

correction

The multiplicity correction, one of stats::p.adjust.methods, passed to stats::p.adjust(). Default "BH".

ci_level

The confidence level of the intervals, between 0 and 1. Default 0.95.

seed

An integer that makes the split reproducible; used only with select = "split". A random-number state that existed before the call is restored afterwards. Default NULL.

x

For the print() and plot() methods: an outcome_model() result.

...

For the print(), summary() and plot() methods: not used.

object

For summary(): an outcome_model() result.

Value

A net_outcome_model object. print() shows the outcome and family, the number of units (and groups), the number of selected terms, the adjustments, the dropped predictors and the correction, followed by the effect table, and returns its input invisibly. summary() and effects_table() return the effect table without the intercept, rounded to three decimals except the p-values; effects_table() also keeps the intercept, or only the significant terms, on request. plot() returns a ggplot forest plot of the effects (odds ratios for a binomial fit, against a dashed line at no effect), with filled markers for terms whose corrected p-value is below 0.05. The object's fields:

effects

The effect table: a data frame with one row per model term, the intercept and the adjust covariates included, and columns term, estimate, std_error, statistic, ci_lower, ci_upper, p_value and p_adj (NA on the intercept row, which is left out of the correction), plus odds_ratio, or_lower and or_upper for a binomial fit.

model

The fitted model: a glm, or an lme4 fit when a random intercept was added.

family

"binomial" or "gaussian".

n

The number of rows the reported model was fitted on.

n_groups

The number of groups; NA unless a random intercept was fitted.

selected

The predictors in the reported model.

dropped

The predictors dropped as non-numeric or constant.

adjust, select, correction, ci_level, outcome

The settings used.

mixed

Whether a random intercept was fitted.

Details

Ordinary gaussian fits use Student t confidence limits with the model's residual degrees of freedom; binomial and mixed fits use normal (Wald) limits. A linear mixed model (lme4::lmer()) reports no p-values, so they are computed from the normal distribution of its t statistics.

Honest inference

Choosing predictors by their association with the outcome and then testing them on the same rows invalidates the p-values. With select = "split" the data is halved: predictors are ranked on one half and the reported model is fitted on the other, so the returned inference is valid for the selected set. select = "none" (default) fits every supplied predictor and needs no split.

See also

simplicial_features, effects_table

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  hint    = rbinom(300, 1, 0.4),
  think   = rbinom(300, 1, 0.3),
  n_events = rpois(300, 20),
  actor   = rep(letters[1:10], each = 30)
)
d$success <- rbinom(300, 1, plogis(-0.5 + 0.8 * d$hint))
fit <- outcome_model(d, outcome = "success",
                     predictors = c("hint", "think"),
                     adjust = "n_events")
effects_table(fit)
#>       term estimate std_error statistic ci_lower ci_upper     p_value
#> 1 n_events    0.064     0.026     2.434    0.012    0.115 0.014937387
#> 2     hint    0.635     0.245     2.591    0.155    1.116 0.009562848
#> 3    think   -0.048     0.258    -0.188   -0.555    0.458 0.851074699
#>        p_adj odds_ratio or_lower or_upper
#> 1 0.02240608      1.066    1.012    1.122
#> 2 0.02240608      1.888    1.167    3.053
#> 3 0.85107470      0.953    0.574    1.580
